$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of the W3C Recommendation Securing Verifiable Credentials using JOSE and COSE (REC-vc-jose-cose-20250515), which prints no JSON Schema, CDDL or ABNF of its own. Source .cache/w3c-vc-jose-cose.bin, sha256 6c70cf8d7de9d8a3ff28a743fea9d569a67a402111c3245fdafbaa2ad6709af9; quotations of the source are checked against its rendering .cache/w3c-vc-jose-cose.txt, sha256 f02bd4966800863d533746c6c39ad267ada1b8bfcbb92186c204b617bb46c126. Quotations of other documents are checked against the copies README.md lists with their digests. INSTANCE MODEL (inferred, this library's, not the source's): a decoded SD-JWT, {compact, issuerSignedJwt: {header, payload}, disclosures: [decoded arrays], keyBindingJwt: {header, payload}}; keyBindingJwt is absent when there is no KB-JWT, and compact is optional. LEVELS. The root and every anchor not ending in -should state MUST and MUST NOT rules: a failure is non-conformance. A rule marked imported is a MUST of another document, named with the clause of this source that makes it bind. Anchors ending in -should add the SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED and NOT RECOMMENDED statements and include the MUST level by reference: a failure there is a deviation from a recommendation, to be reported as a warning, never as non-conformance. A constraint marked inferred is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source. PROFILES: #vc-should, #vp-should. The source defers the format to [SD-JWT] (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0007, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0027, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0030, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0033, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0036, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0042), cited as an Internet-Draft with no revision; what is imported here is read from RFC 9901 (November 2025), its published form. The JSON serialization (application/sd-jwt+json, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0043, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0044) is not modelled: no example uses it. Rules that need digests computed (each disclosure's digest present once, its position) are SD-JWT verification (§5.2 defers to [SD-JWT]) and are not schema rules.
title: SD-JWT-secured credential or presentation, decoded (DERIVED)

compact.$comment: imported through w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0027 and w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0033: the compact serialization, RFC 9901 §4, “SD-JWT = JWT "~" *(DISCLOSURE "~")” (RFC 9901 §4) and “SD-JWT-KB = SD-JWT KB-JWT” (RFC 9901 §4), every segment a non-empty base64url string. The source's own words: “These parts are separated by tilde (~) characters.” (§1.1.2.2) and “If the KB-JWT is not present, the SD-JWT must end with a tilde (~) character.” (§1.1.2.2). A string ending in <KB-JWT>~ fails (Example 22). “Implementations MUST support the compact serialization (application/sd-jwt)” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0042); the JSON serialization w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0043 permits is not modelled.

issuerSignedJwt.$comment: RFC 9901 §4.1 (imported): a signed JWT, never alg none (jose-header.derived).

payload.description: The payload of the Issuer-signed JWT, before disclosures are applied.

_sd_alg.$comment: RFC 9901 §4.1.1 (imported): a string, at the top level only.

_sd.$comment: RFC 9901 §4.2.4.1 and §4.1 (imported): digests of disclosures, base64url, none twice.

payload.$comment: w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0006 holds of the claims an SD-JWT carries in plaintext too. A vc or vp claim hidden in a disclosure surfaces only in the rebuilt claims set, which payload.derived#jwt checks (cross-field-rules.derived.yaml X-09).

sdValue.description: Any JSON value below the top level of an Issuer-signed SD-JWT payload.

then.$comment: imported, RFC 9901: an _sd member is an array of digests (§4.2.4.1, “The _sd key MUST refer to an array of strings, each string being a digest of a Disclosure or a decoy digest as described in Section 4.2.5.” (RFC 9901 §4.2.4.1)), with no digest twice in it (§4.1, “The same digest value MUST NOT appear more than once in the SD-JWT.” (RFC 9901 §4.1); repeats across different arrays are not caught here), and _sd_alg may not appear below the top level (§4.1.1, “When used, this claim MUST appear at the top level of the SD-JWT payload.” (RFC 9901 §4.1.1)).

arrayDigest.$comment: imported, RFC 9901 §4.2.4.2: an array element digest is {"...": <digest>}; “There MUST NOT be any other keys in the object.” (RFC 9901 §4.2.4.2)

disclosure.description: A decoded Disclosure: the JSON array a base64url Disclosure string decodes to.

oneOf.$comment: object property, imported from RFC 9901 §4.2.1: [salt, claim name, claim value]; “A salt value. MUST be a string.” (RFC 9901 §4.2.1); the claim name: “It MUST be a string and MUST NOT be _sd, ..., or a claim name existing in the object as a permanently disclosed claim.” (RFC 9901 §4.2.1) (the clash with a permanently disclosed claim needs the payload and is not checked here). The source's own description says the arrays contain “the digest of the disclosed claim, the claim name, and the claim value.” (§1.1.2.2); read literally, the first element is a digest, while RFC 9901 makes it a salt, and so does the next item of the same list: “Each disclosable claim is combined with a salt value before hashing to prevent dictionary attacks.” (§1.1.2.2). Every one of the 35 disclosures printed in the examples carries a salt there (README.md, Findings). The schema is the same under either reading, since both are strings.
array element, imported from RFC 9901 §4.2.2: [salt, value]; “The array MUST contain two elements in this order:” (RFC 9901 §4.2.2) The source does not describe this form.

kbJwt.description: The Key Binding JWT, decoded. The source says only that it is optional (§1.1.2.2); its shape is imported from RFC 9901 §4.3.

header.$comment: RFC 9901 §4.3 (imported): “typ: REQUIRED. MUST be kb+jwt” (RFC 9901 §4.3); alg REQUIRED and “It MUST NOT be "none".” (RFC 9901 §4.3)

payload.$comment: RFC 9901 §4.3 (imported): iat, aud, nonce and sd_hash REQUIRED. aud: “The value MUST be a single string that identifies the intended receiver of the Key Binding JWT.” (RFC 9901 §4.3) nonce: “The value type of this claim MUST be a string.” (RFC 9901 §4.3) sd_hash: “sd_hash: REQUIRED.” (RFC 9901 §4.3) Example 22's KB-JWT has no sd_hash and fails here (README.md, Findings).

plain.description: A JSON value with nothing selectively disclosable inside it: no _sd member and no {"...": <digest>} element at any depth.

vcShould.description: application/vc+sd-jwt, SHOULD level (§3.2.1). Includes the root.
vcShould.$comment: SHOULD: “implementers SHOULD ensure that properties necessary for the validation and verification of a credential are NOT selectively disclosable” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0031); the list that follows it names @context, type, credentialStatus, credentialSchema, relatedResource. Checked without computing digests (inferred, this library's reading of an open list): @context and type are in the Issuer-signed payload in plaintext; the five, where present in plaintext, hold nothing selectively disclosable (#plain); and no object-property disclosure is named @context, credentialStatus, credentialSchema or relatedResource. A disclosure named type cannot be placed without its digest, since type also names members at other depths; the plaintext-type check covers the top level, and cross-field-rules.derived.yaml X-08 places every disclosure by digest. Examples 4, 18 and 19 disclose the credential's own type selectively and fail here (README.md, Findings).

vpShould.description: application/vp+sd-jwt, SHOULD level (§3.2.2). Includes the root.
vpShould.$comment: SHOULD: “implementers SHOULD ensure that properties necessary for the validation and verification of a credential are NOT selectively disclosable” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0040); the list that follows it names @context, type, credentialStatus, credentialSchema, relatedResource. Checked without computing digests (inferred, this library's reading of an open list): @context and type are in the Issuer-signed payload in plaintext; the five, where present in plaintext, hold nothing selectively disclosable (#plain); and no object-property disclosure is named @context, credentialStatus, credentialSchema or relatedResource. A disclosure named type cannot be placed without its digest, since type also names members at other depths; the plaintext-type check covers the top level, and cross-field-rules.derived.yaml X-08 places every disclosure by digest. Examples 5, 6 and 20 disclose the presentation's own type selectively and fail here; applying the five names to the presentation's own members is inferred, since the sentence, in a section about presentations, speaks of a credential (README.md, Findings).
